Things 91–97: Leadership, Collaboration, and Responsibility

第 10 章（共 10 章）：领导力、协作与责任（第 91–97 篇）

91. When Our Data Science Team Didn't Produce Value当我们的数据科学团队没有产出价值时

Joel Nantais

乔尔·南泰斯

I'm in my boss's office, briefing him on the new dashboard that will greatly increase access to data for everyone in the organization. Like a slap in the face, he says, "Your data team can't get any meaningful data."

我在老板办公室，向他汇报新仪表盘，说它将极大提升组织中每个人对数据的访问。像被当面扇了一耳光，他说：“你们数据团队拿不出任何有意义的数据。”

To say that this caught me off guard is an understatement. I knew the team was working hard. We had designed and launched several complex projects over the years. Yet he didn't have confidence in our data or our ability to provide value. Genuinely confused, I probed to learn more about his experience and perspective. He needed urgent, reactive responses to his data requests. Constantly, he heard we couldn't provide the data.

说这事让我猝不及防都是轻描淡写。我知道团队在努力工作。这些年我们设计并上线了好几个复杂项目。然而他对我们的数据、对我们提供价值的能力没有信心。我真的很困惑，于是追问他的经历和视角。他需要对数据请求做紧急、被动的响应。他不断听到我们说拿不出数据。

The priorities of the data team had focused on BI, ML, and forecasting tools. These were where the organization needed to be and had justified the increase in resources. Heck, we were following the five-year plan!

数据团队的优先级聚焦在 BI、ML 和预测工具上。这些是组织应该在的方向，也为资源增长提供了理由。见鬼，我们可是在按五年计划走！

Looking back, I overfocused on the progress of our "sexy" long-term initiatives. And ad hoc data requests were not a priority. Only those requests with easy data access were fulfilled.

回头看，我过度聚焦于我们“性感”长期项目的进展。即席数据请求不是优先级。只有那些数据容易拿的请求被满足了。

When you are in a reactive organization, you need to devote resources to that mission. I was determined to change the perception of our usefulness. We worked to ensure that the team set a new culture of "getting to yes" no matter the effort. We reprioritized projects and held each other accountable.

当你处在一个被动反应型组织里，你需要为那个使命投入资源。我决心改变人们对我们有用性的看法。我们努力让团队建立一种无论花多大力气都“说 yes”的新文化。我们重新排了项目优先级，彼此问责。

Before this experience, we didn't have an exploration mindset. This was my fault. I had delegated specific tasks and requests without spending time to set expectations. I trusted my team members' expertise (correctly) but didn't explore the why for declined requests (incorrectly).

在这次经历之前，我们没有探索型思维。这是我的错。我把具体任务和请求分派下去，却没花时间设预期。我信任团队成员的专业能力（这是对的），但没有去探索被拒请求背后的 why（这是错的）。

— p.209 —

As a leader, it isn't enough to build the right team. You also have to form the right attitude and culture. You have to allow the needs of the organization to set the priorities.

作为领导，光建对团队不够。你还必须形成对的态度和文化。你必须让组织的需求来设定优先级。

How can you turn it around? If this sounds at all similar to the organization you work in, I recommend the following:

你怎么扭转局面？如果你工作的组织听起来有点类似，我建议以下几点：

  • Five whys. This is my favorite tool. It allows you to push the team to understand true limitations.
    五个为什么。这是我最喜欢的工具。它让你推动团队理解真正的局限。
  • Stakeholder engagement. Spend significant time with requesters to understand needs. Engage a larger stakeholder group to get inconvenient data.
    利益相关者参与。花大量时间和请求者在一起理解需求。让更大的利益相关者群体参与，去拿那些不方便的数据。
  • Domain knowledge. Help the team lean on the subject-matter experts (SMEs), and make the discussions a two-way street. Show them your data, and have them walk you through their processes.
    领域知识。帮助团队依靠主题专家（SME），让讨论成为双向道。给他们看你的数据，让他们带你走一遍他们的流程。
  • External awareness. Get out of your office. Talk to the people in other offices. Understand their needs and wants.
    外部感知。走出你的办公室。和其他办公室的人聊聊。理解他们的需求和想要什么。

In organizations that are not built around data science, you need to understand how your work contributes to the overall mission. When in a support role, have a genuine concern about the organization's needs and problems. Understand how your tools can provide solutions. Balance long-term solutions with short-term needs. Usually, today's problem matters more than next year's problem.

在不是围绕数据科学建起来的组织里，你需要理解你的工作如何贡献于整体使命。当你在支持角色时，要真正关心组织的需求和问题。理解你的工具能如何提供解决方案。在长期方案与短期需求之间平衡。通常，今天的问题比明年的问题更重要。

— p.210 —

92. When to Avoid the Naive Approach什么时候该避免天真做法

Nimrod Parasol

尼姆罗德·帕拉索尔

They always say you should avoid overengineering. You just started the project and have no way of knowing what the future holds, so you should make the solution as simple as possible. Don't try to solve problems that do not exist yet. But sometimes the cost of postponing problems for later might be too high.

人们总说你应该避免过度工程。你刚启动项目，无从知道未来会怎样，所以应该让解决方案尽可能简单。别去解决还不存在的问题。但有时把问题推迟到以后的代价可能太高。

When you deal with large amounts of data, you find out that data migrations are complicated and costly processes. You need to write the code that transforms data from the old to the new format, then you need to run it over all your existing data, and eventually you need to perfectly synchronize the old and the new datasets in real time, so that consumers won't notice any change. This process is expensive in employee power and computer power and always carries the risk of introducing bugs into your production system.

当你处理大量数据时，会发现数据迁移是复杂而昂贵的过程。你需要写代码把数据从旧格式转换到新格式，然后需要在所有现有数据上跑，最终需要实时完美同步新旧数据集，让消费方察觉不到变化。这个过程在人力和算力上都很贵，并且总带着把 bug 引入生产系统的风险。

When you design your data store, you should think about how to avoid data migrations in the future. There are two main factors to consider.

设计数据存储时，你应该思考如何在未来避免数据迁移。有两个主要因素要考虑。

The first is the data storage format. It might be a database, or the file format you choose to use in your data lake. Once you decide on one, changing it will require either having a complicated system that supports both the old and new formats, or doing a data migration. Both are unwanted.

第一个是数据存储格式。它可能是数据库，也可能是你在数据湖中选择用的文件格式。一旦选定，要改它就需要要么有一个同时支持新旧格式的复杂系统，要么做一次数据迁移。两者都不想要。

The second aspect to consider is the partition's schema. Most data stores today support schema evolution of some sort. You'll be able to add or remove fields fairly easily. But when you change the fields that partition the data, you have to migrate the data to the new partitions.

第二个要考虑的是分区 schema。今天大多数数据存储支持某种 schema 演进。你能相当容易地加或删字段。但当你改变用来分区数据的字段时，就必须把数据迁移到新分区。

You might think that for starters, it'll be enough to use the company's default database technology without any partitioning. This might be true, but if you stop and consider these two points beforehand, you might notice optimizations that you already know you'll need to do in the future. So why not get rid of those right off the bat?

你可能觉得一开始用公司默认数据库技术、不做分区就够了。这可能是对的，但如果你事先停下来考虑这两点，可能会注意到那些你已经知道未来需要做的优化。那为什么不一开始就把它们解决掉呢？

— p.211 —

As with most things, there is no single universal truth. It might make sense to start with an un-optimized data store. Maybe it's still possible the project will never make it to production. Maybe you don't have any information about the expected query patterns, but need to quickly create a prototype.

和大多数事一样，没有唯一的普世真理。用未优化的数据存储起步可能合理。也许项目根本不会上线。也许你对预期查询模式一无所知、但需要快速做个原型。

When you do decide to go with the naive approach, you should know that if you let too much data accumulate before the optimizations, it will be expensive to do them later. In that case, it's best to mark milestones (either by data volume or business status) for revisiting the design before it becomes too late.

当你确实决定采用天真做法时，应该知道：如果在优化前积累了太多数据，以后再做就会很贵。这种情况下，最好标记里程碑（按数据量或业务状态），好在为时已晚之前重访设计。

— p.212 —

93. When to Be Cautious About Sharing Data什么时候该谨慎共享数据

Thomas Nield

托马斯·尼尔德

When I was fresh out of business school, I was taught that silos are bad and even toxic to organizations. When people and departments become too secluded and inwardly focused, all kinds of corporate dysfunction can happen. Redundant work becomes commonplace, contradicting and competing objectives undermine the efficacy of the organization, and valuable data that could benefit everyone stays locked away with its owners.

我刚从商学院毕业时，被教导说孤岛对组织不好、甚至有毒。当人和部门变得过于封闭、向内看时，各种组织功能失调就会发生。重复劳动变得普遍，相互矛盾和竞争的目标损害组织效能，能让所有人受益的宝贵数据被锁在其所有者手里。

While these concerns are valid and do happen, I have learned that bureaucracy and silos sometimes exist for legitimate reasons. Data can become a political and organizational headache if it is made available to too many parties. "Why?" you ask in a surprised tone. "Shouldn't transparency and open data drive analysis and innovations?" Well, of course, but making data available is a balancing act and depends on the situation.

虽然这些关切是对的、也确实会发生，但我学到：官僚和孤岛有时是有正当理由存在的。如果把数据开放给太多方，数据会变成政治和组织上的头疼事。“为什么？”你惊讶地问。“透明度和开放数据不应该驱动分析和创新吗？”当然应该，但开放数据是一种平衡术，取决于具体情况。

Let's get the obvious reasons that you should not share data out of the way first. If the data is sensitive, it is best to give access on only a need-to-know basis. If the database is vulnerable to heavy traffic and expensive analytical SQL queries, that is another obvious reason to not provide access. Typically, in that situation, you would provide a replicated database used for analysis, so it does not impact the production database.

我们先把那些显然不该共享数据的理由摆出来。如果数据敏感，最好按需要知道的原则授权。如果数据库容易受大流量和昂贵分析 SQL 查询的冲击，那是另一个显然不该授权的理由。通常这种情况下，你会提供一个复制出来的数据库用于分析，不影响生产数据库。

Now I want to get into a less obvious reason: sometimes domain experts should have exclusive access to a database and be its gatekeepers. I know this sounds bureaucratic and terrible, and I too hate the phrase "leave it to the experts." But bear with me.

现在我想讲一个不那么明显的理由：有时领域专家应该对数据库有独占访问权、当它的看门人。我知道这听起来官僚又糟糕，我也讨厌“交给专家”这种说法。但请听我说完。

Sometimes navigating and interpreting specialized data correctly can be difficult, because doing so requires an immense amount of domain knowledge. If you know nothing about revenue forecasting, do you really have any business going through a revenue-forecasting database? Maybe you should ask the revenue-forecasting people directly for what you need! They know that data, the business it reflects, and which fields require a WHERE condition for your inquiry.

有时正确地导航和解读专业数据可能很难，因为这需要海量领域知识。如果你对收入预测一无所知，你真有什么理由去翻一个收入预测数据库吗？也许你应该直接问收入预测的人要你需要的东西！他们了解那份数据、它反映的业务、以及你查询时哪些字段需要 WHERE 条件。

— p.213 —

Say Joe works for a Fortune 500 company and transitions from one department to another. His new department asks if he can pull some strings to help get access to forecasting data from his previous department. Joe rightly tells them the implications of what they are asking for: the data is complicated and requires full-time expertise to interpret. It is not the type of database to browse casually, and it is easy to query incorrectly.

假设 Joe 在一家财富 500 公司工作，从一个部门转到另一个部门。他的新部门问他能不能走走门路，帮忙从他以前部门拿到预测数据。Joe 正确地告诉他们这个请求的含义：数据很复杂，需要全职专业知识来解读。它不是那种可以随便浏览的数据库，很容易查错。

Not to mention, if Joe's new department starts doing his old department's work—well, that's going to complicate their organization, and this will perhaps step on some toes. When it comes to forecasting work, where should budget and talent be put now? Both departments? At best this may be a necessary organizational change, but at worst it can be a bitter and unnecessary political struggle.

更不用说，如果 Joe 的新部门开始做他老部门的工作——那会让他们的组织变复杂，也许还会踩到一些脚趾。说到预测工作，预算和人才现在应该投到哪里？两个部门都投？最好情况下这可能是必要的组织变革，但最坏情况下它可能是一场痛苦而不必要的政治斗争。

Delegating responsibilities (and the data that goes with it) in an organization is no easy task. Centralizing data and making it accessible to as many stakeholders as possible is a noble objective, but it's not always practical. Some data should be shared more openly, while other data should be exclusively kept with its full-time experts who know it intimately enough to use it correctly.

在一个组织里分派责任（以及随之而来的数据）不是易事。把数据集中起来、让尽可能多利益相关者访问，是一个崇高目标，但它并不总是实际。有些数据应该更开放地共享，而另一些数据应该独占性地留给那些全职专家——他们对数据足够熟，才能正确使用它。

— p.214 —

94. When to Talk and When to Listen什么时候该说话，什么时候该倾听

Steven Finkelstein

史蒂文·芬克尔斯坦

As we approach the one-year anniversary on my current digitization project at work, I look back to see what can be learned from the experience. Project SWIFT was aimed at providing information about my employer's global manufacturing plants to the product developers earlier in the development process. The output would be a data-collection tool and a business intelligence report in Tableau. The objective was quite simple, but we encountered constant obstacles at the micro and macro level.

在我目前工作的数字化项目快满一年之际，我回头看看能从这段经历中学到什么。SWIFT 项目旨在：在开发过程更早阶段，向产品开发者提供我雇主全球制造工厂的信息。产出将是一个数据采集工具和一份 Tableau 商业智能报表。目标相当简单，但我们在微观和宏观层面都不断遇到障碍。

At the macro level, huge shifts were occurring in our organization. Our department was undergoing a strategic shift to the cloud and becoming more data driven. Significant organizational restructures happened, including the creation of a new data analytics team that absorbed my position. For new projects such as SWIFT, my team took the lead on the technical side, as opposed to IT in prior years. The organizational changes left a gap in leadership for critical design decisions. I believe this macro-level change was the foundation for the many challenges this project faced.

宏观层面，我们组织正在发生巨大转变。我们部门正在战略转向云、变得更数据驱动。发生了重大组织重组，包括新建一个数据分析团队并吸收了我的岗位。对 SWIFT 这类新项目，是我的团队而不是往年的 IT 在技术方面牵头。组织变化让关键设计决策在领导上出现空白。我相信这个宏观变化是这个项目面临许多挑战的基础。

At the micro level, I was at the center of all requirements discussions. The data required for the final report did not exist, so early conversations were about what data needed to be captured, and the relationships between the entities being modeled. The initial request was translated into 35 data fields. Immediately, I pushed back against this request. We were employing an Agile methodology to get this project live as swiftly as possible. But as soon as we agreed on fewer fields, we hit a major obstacle.

微观层面，我在所有需求讨论的中心。最终报表所需的数据并不存在，所以早期对话是关于要采集什么数据、以及被建模实体之间的关系。最初的请求被翻译成 35 个数据字段。我立刻反对这个请求。我们在采用敏捷方法，以尽快让项目上线。但我们刚同意减少字段，就遇到一个大障碍。

The project added new subject-matter experts with more specialized knowledge. This resulted in previous requirements being questioned. Every ensuing meeting had 10 or more people attending. You had to be selective about which questions to ask and how to present the requests clearly. I remember constantly tweaking my approach to uncover which pairs of data fields had a many-to-many relationship. Sometimes my requests were interpreted incorrectly, but it was never entirely clear when I should enter a conversation. The best I could do was listen and wait for the right opening to correct the course.

项目加入了新的、有更专业知识的主题专家。这导致以前的需求被质疑。之后每次会议都有 10 人以上参加。你必须有选择地问哪些问题、以及如何清晰地呈现请求。我记得不断调整我的方法，去揭示哪几对数据字段之间有多对多关系。有时我的请求被错误理解，但我完全不清楚什么时候该插入对话。我能做的最好的事，就是倾听、等待正确的开口时机来纠正航向。

— p.215 —

As of today, we are still working on the project, but I am happy to say that we are live. While some ongoing challenges remain, we have made significant progress. The scope of the project was reduced to nine fields, and we designed the data model in third normal form to maximize flexibility for the business. Without the constant pushback from our team to reduce the complexity of the project, we would be nowhere near "go live."

到今天我们还在做这个项目，但我很高兴地说我们已经上线。虽然还有一些持续挑战，我们已取得显著进展。项目范围缩减到 9 个字段，我们按第三范式设计数据模型，以最大化业务灵活性。如果没有我们团队不断抵制以降低项目复杂度，我们离“上线”差得远。

This project provided many valuable lessons. Aiming for simplicity is essential in all discussions; however, understanding when it is our time to talk versus listen is extremely subjective. Steve Jobs said it best: "Our job is to figure out what they're going to want before they do." As a data engineer, sometimes you need to think like Steve Jobs in order to guide various stakeholders down the right path of technical simplicity, while still addressing their requirements.

这个项目给了许多宝贵教训。在所有讨论中追求简单都是必要的；然而判断什么时候该我们说、什么时候该听，极其主观。史蒂夫·乔布斯说得最好：“我们的工作是在他们想要之前想出来他们会想要什么。”作为数据工程师，有时你需要像乔布斯一样思考，才能引导各利益相关者走上技术简单的正确道路，同时仍然满足他们的需求。

— p.216 —

95. Why Data Science Teams Need Generalists, Not Specialists为什么数据科学团队需要通才而非专才

Eric Colson

埃里克·科尔森

In The Wealth of Nations, Adam Smith demonstrates how the division of labor is the chief source of productivity gains, using the vivid example of a pin factory assembly line: "One person draws out the wire, another straightens it, a third cuts it, a fourth points it, a fifth grinds it." With specialization oriented around function, each worker becomes highly skilled in a narrow task, leading to process efficiencies.

在《国富论》中，亚当·斯密用别针厂流水线这个生动例子展示了劳动分工如何是生产率提升的主要来源：“一个人抽铁丝，另一个拉直，第三个切，第四个磨尖，第五个抛光。”以职能为导向的专业化，让每个工人在狭窄任务上高度熟练，带来流程效率。

The allure of such efficiencies has led us to organize even our data science teams by specialty functions such as data engineers, machine learning engineers, research scientists, causal inference scientists, and so on. Specialists' work is coordinated by a product manager, with handoffs between the functions in a manner resembling the pin factory: "one person sources the data, another models it, a third implements it, a fourth measures it," and on and on.

这种效率的诱惑，让我们甚至把数据科学团队也按专业职能组织起来：数据工程师、机器学习工程师、研究科学家、因果推断科学家等等。专才的工作由产品经理协调，职能之间像别针厂一样交接：“一个人找数据，另一个建模，第三个实现，第四个度量”，如此循环。

The challenge with this approach is that data science products and services can rarely be designed up front. They need to be learned and developed via iteration. Yet, when development is distributed among multiple specialists, several forces can hamper iteration cycles. Coordination costs—the time spent communicating, discussing, and justifying each change—scale proportionally with the number of people involved.

这种方法的挑战在于：数据科学产品和服务很少能预先设计。它们需要通过迭代来学习和发展。然而，当开发被分给多个专才时，几股力量会妨碍迭代周期。协调成本——花在沟通、讨论、为每次变更辩护上的时间——随涉及人数成比例增长。

Even with just a few specialists, the cost of coordinating their work can quickly exceed any benefit from their division of labor. Even more nefarious are the wait times that elapse between the units of work performed by the specialists. Schedules of specialists are difficult to align, so projects often sit idle, waiting for specialists' resources to become available. These two forces can impair iteration, which is critical to the development of data science products. Status updates like "waiting on ETL changes" or "waiting on ML Eng for implementation" are common symptoms that you have overspecialized.

即使只有几个专才，协调他们工作的成本也可能很快超过劳动分工的任何收益。更恶劣的是专才完成各工作单元之间的等待时间。专才的日程难以对齐，所以项目常常空转，等专才资源可用。这两股力量会损害迭代——而迭代对数据科学产品开发至关重要。像“等 ETL 变更”或“等 ML 工程实现”这类状态更新，是你过度专业化的常见症状。

— p.217 —

Instead of organizing data scientists by specialty function, give each end-to-end ownership for different business capabilities. For example, one data scientist can build a product-recommendation capability, a second can build a customer-prospecting capability, and so on. Each data scientist will then perform all the functions required to develop each capability, from model training to ETL to implementation to measurement.

与其按专业职能组织数据科学家，不如让每个人端到端拥有不同的业务能力。例如，一个数据科学家可以建产品推荐能力，第二个可以建客户挖掘能力，等等。每个数据科学家将执行开发该能力所需的所有职能：从模型训练到 ETL、到实现、到度量。

Of course, these data scientist generalists have to perform their work sequentially rather than in parallel. However, doing the work typically takes just a fraction of the wait time required for separate specialist resources to become available. So, iteration and development time goes down. Learning and development are faster.

当然，这些数据科学通才必须顺序而不是并行地做工作。然而，实际做工作通常只需要分开的专才资源等到可用所需等待时间的一小部分。于是迭代和开发时间下降。学习和发展更快。

Many find this notion of full-stack data science generalists to be daunting. Particularly, it's the technical skills that most find so challenging to acquire, as many data scientists have not been trained as software engineers. However, much of the technical complexity can be abstracted away through a robust data platform. Data scientists can be shielded from the inner workings of containerization, distributed processing, and automatic failover. This allows the data scientists to focus more on the science side of things, learning and developing solutions through iteration.

许多人觉得全栈数据科学通才这个概念令人生畏。尤其是技术技能，大多数人觉得难以掌握，因为许多数据科学家没有受过软件工程师训练。然而，许多技术复杂度可以通过健壮的数据平台抽象掉。数据科学家可以被屏蔽掉容器化、分布式处理、自动故障转移的内部运作。这让数据科学家能更聚焦于科学那一面，通过迭代学习和发展解决方案。

— p.218 —

96. With Great Data Comes Great Responsibility数据越大，责任越大

Lohit VijayaRenu

洛希特·维贾亚雷努

The past decade has seen an explosion of data, affecting the way it is collected, processed, and analyzed at various organizations to better serve their customers. Many have embraced this change to become data-first companies. Both hardware and software systems have evolved to support big data systems, making it easy for data engineers to derive valuable insights that were never possible before. While data-driven applications have improved the user experience, user information can be exposed to applications and users beyond their control. Data engineers should now treat this information with greater responsibility.

过去十年见证了数据的爆炸，影响了各组织收集、处理和分析数据以更好服务客户的方式。许多组织拥抱这种变化，成为数据优先公司。硬件和软件系统都已演进以支持大数据系统，让数据工程师能轻松提取以前不可能得到的有价值洞见。虽然数据驱动的应用改善了用户体验，但用户信息可能暴露给他们控制之外的应用和用户。数据工程师现在应以更大的责任感对待这些信息。

Put Yourself in the User's Shoes设身处地为用户着想

Multiple systems collect various kinds of personal information about users. Always handle users' information as you would your own. Data engineers should sometimes act as data guardians while designing data applications. We should always follow company or industry standards around security and privacy. An organization should have dedicated people or teams who help enforce security policies while making sure they are up-to-date against newer threats.

多个系统收集用户各种个人信息。永远像对待你自己的信息一样对待用户信息。数据工程师在设计数据应用时，有时应该扮演数据守护者。我们应始终遵守公司或行业在安全和隐私方面的标准。组织应有专门的人或团队帮忙执行安全策略，同时确保策略针对新威胁是最新的。

Ensure Ethical Use of User Information确保合乎伦理地使用用户信息

Even with all the security policies enforced, it is the professional responsibility of data engineers to make sure user data is consumed in ethical ways. Advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms can easily predict user behavior and intent. We have to take time to think more about the implications of these algorithms and how they affect users' experiences and emotions.

即使所有安全策略都被执行，确保用户数据以合乎伦理的方式被消费，仍是数据工程师的职业责任。高级机器学习和 AI 算法可以轻松预测用户行为和意图。我们必须花时间更多地思考这些算法的含义、以及它们如何影响用户的体验和情绪。

— p.219 —

Watch Your Data Footprint注意你的数据足迹

As you build applications that consume data, you should also watch for how the output of your application is used. It is our responsibility to understand where and how the generated data is used, who has access to it, and what kinds of downstream applications are built using this data. This is also true if you are consuming data derived from other applications. Try to understand the intended usage and make an effort to expose its use to the original creator.

当你构建消费数据的应用时，你也应该留意你的应用输出是如何被使用的。我们有责任理解：生成的数据在哪里、如何被使用，谁能访问它，以及基于它构建了哪些下游应用。如果你消费从其他应用派生的数据，这也成立。试着理解预期用途，并努力把它的使用情况暴露给最初的创建者。

It is now more important than ever before for organizations to have a holistic view of how user information is used, what is derived from it, and who has access to this information.

现在比以往任何时候都更重要的是：组织对用户信息如何被使用、从中派生出什么、谁能访问这些信息，要有一个整体视图。

— p.220 —

97. Your Data Tests Failed! Now What?你的数据测试挂了！接下来怎么办？

Sam Bail, PhD

萨姆·贝尔 博士

Congratulations—you've successfully implemented data testing in your pipeline! Whether that's using an off-the-shelf tool or home-cooked validation code, you've taken the crucial steps to ensuring high-quality data insights. But do you also have a plan for what happens when your tests actually fail? In this chapter, we'll talk through some key stages of responding to data test failures and critical questions to ask when developing a data-quality strategy for your team.

恭喜——你已经在管道里成功实现了数据测试！无论是用现成工具还是自己写的校验代码，你已经迈出了确保高质量数据洞见的关键几步。但你有没有一个计划：当测试真的失败时怎么办？本章我们讨论应对数据测试失败的几个关键阶段，以及为团队制定数据质量策略时要问的关键问题。

System Response系统响应

Automated system responses are the first line of response to a failed data test. This could be either doing nothing, isolating "bad" data and continuing the pipeline, or stopping the pipeline.

自动化系统响应是数据测试失败的第一道响应线。它可以是：什么都不做、隔离“坏”数据并继续管道、或停止管道。

Logging and Alerting日志与告警

Which errors need alerting and which ones can simply be logged for later use? Which medium (email, Slack, PagerDuty, etc.) do you choose for the alerts to make sure they get noticed? When are they sent (instantaneously, at the end of a pipeline run, or at a fixed time)? And finally, are the alerts clear enough for the responders to understand what happened and the severity of the incident?

哪些错误需要告警、哪些只需记日志以后看？你选哪种媒介（邮件、Slack、PagerDuty 等）发告警以确保被注意？什么时候发（即时、管道跑完时、还是固定时间）？最后，告警是否足够清晰，让响应者理解发生了什么、事件的严重程度？

Alert Response告警响应

Who will see and respond to those notifications? Is there an on-call rotation? What is the agreed-upon response time? And do all stakeholders know who owns the response?

谁会看到并响应这些通知？有没有值班轮班？约定的响应时间是多少？所有利益相关者都知道谁负责响应吗？

— p.221 —

Stakeholder Communication利益相关者沟通

You'll want to let data consumers know that "something is up with the data" before they notice. While investigating the issue, it is also helpful to keep an open line of communication with stakeholders to provide updates on the issue-resolution process.

你会想在数据消费方注意到之前告诉他们“数据出了点事”。在调查问题期间，与利益相关者保持开放沟通渠道、提供问题解决过程的更新，也很有帮助。

Root Cause Identification根因识别

The key to identifying the root cause of data issues is to be methodical about the following:

识别数据问题根因的关键是：有条理地做下面这些事：

  • Identifying the exact issue that's actually happening
    识别实际发生的确切问题
  • Identifying the cause of the issue
    识别问题的原因

I recommend not taking test failures at face value. For example, a test for null values in a column could fail because some rows have actual null values or because that column no longer exists. It makes sense to dig into the cause of an issue only after it's clear what that issue actually is!

我建议不要按表面意思接受测试失败。例如，一个列空值测试失败，可能因为某些行真的有空值，也可能因为该列已经不存在了。只有在清楚问题到底是什么之后，再去挖它的原因才有意义！

Issue Resolution问题解决

We can organize the issues causing data test failures into the following categories:

我们可以把导致数据测试失败的问题归为以下几类：

  • The data is actually correct, but the tests need to be adjusted. This can happen when there are unusual, but correct, outliers.
    数据其实是对的，但测试需要调整。当有不寻常但正确的离群点时会发生这种情况。
  • The data is "broken" but can be fixed. For example, we might have incorrectly formatted phone numbers. In this case, we can make the respective changes in the upstream data, if we have access, or add logic in the pipeline code to handle these issues.
    数据“坏了”但可以修。例如，我们可能有格式错误的电话号码。这种情况下，如果能访问上游数据，我们可以在上游做相应修改，或在管道代码中加逻辑处理这些问题。
  • The data is "broken" and can't be fixed. This may happen with missing values, or when we simply don't have access to the source data. In this case, we can choose to isolate the "broken" records and continue running the pipeline without them, or we might have to adjust our downstream use of the data to account for those issues.
    数据“坏了”且修不了。这可能发生在缺失值情况下，或当我们根本访问不到源数据时。这种情况下，我们可以选择隔离“坏”记录、不带它们继续跑管道，或者我们可能必须调整下游对数据的使用来应对这些问题。
— p.222 —
